newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - March 27.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - March 27.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING AND MARKETING:

CHICAGO - Quaker Oats Co says it assigned advertising responsibility for four of its cereal brands to Foote Cone & Belding Chicago, part of True North Communications Inc. Advertising for Quaker Oats oatmeal, Instant Quaker Oatmeal, Life and Quaker 100% Natural cereal brands were switched to Foote Cone from Jordan McGrath Case Taylor, New York.

TOKYO - Japan's expenditure on advertising on major Internet sites is estimated to have totalled some 1.6 billion yen ($12.9 million) in calendar 1996, Japan's leading advertising agency Dentsu Inc reports. Dentsu expects Internet-related advertising to rise to four billion yen in 1997.

WINSTON-SALEM, North Carolina - R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co says the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has not asked any new questions about the company's Joe Camel advertising campaign. The Wall Street Journal reports that FTC staff members are asking the agency to bring an unfair advertising case against the tobacco company for aiming its advertising at youths.
MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:

PARIS - Shares in French pay-television company Canal Plus jump by over 2.5 percent on the back of a company report valuing the assets of merger partner Nethold BV at more than 10 billion francs ($1.8 billion). Canal Plus is set to become Europe's biggest pay-television group on April 15 when it finalises a merger with Dutch-registered media group Nethold.

NEW YORK - Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS Cable will launch the CBS Eye on People cable network on March 31, CBS officials say. The advertiser-supported, 24-hour network will offer entertainment and information programming.

LONDON - Britain's television watchdog, the Independent Television Commission, says Carlton Television breached several codes in its broadcast last December of "Now We're Talking," a special programme funded by British Telecommunications Plc.
LONDON - Good progress has been made in recent months towards the launch of multi-channel digital television in Britain, telecoms watchdog OFTEL says.

REDMOND, Washington - Microsoft Corp unveils its new Internet platform, called Marble, aimed at financial institutions that want to make their sites on the World Wide Web more secure. Marble will help developers create Websites that allow customers to view statements, transfer funds and pay bills online.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS AND MARKETS:

PARIS - Euro Disney's new chairman, Gilles Pelisson, says the sales trend in the first quarter of 1996-97 signalled an "excellent outlook" for the Disneyland Paris theme park in the first half. But Pelisson reiterated that 1997 would be "a difficult year".

ZURICH - Shares in the world's biggest food company, Nestle SA, jump after it reports 1996 group net profit rose 16.6 percent to 3.40 billion Swiss francs ($6.9 billion) and proposed a big boost to its dividend. The operating margin was unchanged at 9.7 percent, even though the group increased advertising and promotional spending to support the launch of new products and increase market share, it said.

CHICAGO - Rawlings Sporting Goods Co, probably best known for baseballs and other sporting equipment, is putting its name on a new line of sport drinks, the company says. The new beverage, Rawlings Sport a New Age, will be introduced in May, followed in June by Rawlings for Kids and Rawlings Natural Spring Water.

EDINBURGH - A rise in Scotch whisky exports to the United States and Japan during 1996 helped offset a decrease in sales within the European Union, the Scotch Whisky Association says. Exports totalled 2.278 billion stg ($3.7 billion) in 1996, up slightly from 2.277 billion in 1995.

CHUP PLANTATION, Cambodia - In Cambodia's oldest rubber plantation, the last remains of a once-great industry trickle slowly from the towering trees. The Cambodian rubber industry, once among the world's most productive, is collapsing under the weight of poor management, corruption and little investment in new trees, analysts say.
SANTIAGO - Chilean supermarket sales grew 4.3 percent in January on the same month last year but fell 1.7 percent in February, says the Chilean Association of Supermarkets.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

DUBAI - The Gulf Arab emirate of Dubai is holding a month-long shop-until-you-drop festival. It is running a global publicity blitz to lure shoppers and tourists. Shopping malls, hotels and restaurants are offering discounts.

WASHINGTON - Age-based ratings like those recently adopted by the United States' television industry entice children to watch programs with a restrictive rating for sex, violence or foul language, according to a new study. "Restricted ratings seem to produce a 'forbidden fruit' effect," says Joanne Cantor of the University of Wisconsin.

CANBERRA - Australia's average room occupancy rate for hotels and motels rose to 59.9 percent in the December quarter 1996 from 59.7 percent in the December quarter of 1995, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports.
